subject: RFI: orchestration scheduling and hotpath fallback plan for migration
messages:
From: Jamie Reynolds <jamie@northbridge.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@northbridge.com
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: RFI: orchestration scheduling and hotpath fallback plan for migration

Ben —

Thanks for the quick onboarding materials earlier. As part of our RFI we need a consolidated, step-by-step plan for how Redwood would orchestrate the migration of our inference traffic from our current vendor to Redwood Dedicated (staged, low-risk approach). Specifically we need: 

- Target timeline (milestones and phase lengths) for a 3-phase migration (staging -> canary -> full cutover)
- Integration steps where our engineering team is required (schema mapping, auth, telemetry hooks)
- Canary criteria and rapid rollback (TTR/TTA targets) for customer-facing endpoints and background batch jobs
- Runbook for the hotpath (latency-sensitive) endpoints and fallback lanes to ensure <100ms p95 after warm-up
- Audit and evidence we can put in the RFP (pre/post test artifacts)

Attaching our security checklist and RFP appendix (Northbridge_RFP_Security_Checklist.xlsx). Can you provide a draft by EOD Tuesday so we can include it in our vendor evaluation packet?

Best,
Jamie Reynolds
Sr. Procurement Manager
Northbridge Financial
[Attachment: Northbridge_RFP_Security_Checklist.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Reynolds <jamie@northbridge.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 10:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: RFI: orchestration scheduling and hotpath fallback plan for migration

Jamie — thanks for the clear ask and the checklist. We can absolutely provide a detailed migration orchestration playbook and the evidence artifacts you need. High-level response below and a draft playbook attached — Redwood_Migration_Playbook_v1.pdf — that contains timelines, runbook steps, and canary criteria. I’ve also included a compact Canary_Criteria.xlsx for your review.

High-level phases (recommended):
1) Staging & validation (2–3 weeks): provisioning in your VPC (if Private), model validation with sample traffic, KV cache warm-up runs, and synthetic load tests.
2) Controlled canary (1 week): route 1–5% production traffic to Redwood Dedicated; parallel metrics comparison and error budget burn assessment.
3) Gradual ramp (2–4 weeks): progressive ramp to 25%, 50%, then full cutover with automated health gates and capacity buffering.

Key integration touchpoints (your team):
- Auth & signing: exchange service account credentials, update token validation (1 day prep)
- Schema mapping: verify request/response schemas and structured output parsers (2–3 days)
- Telemetry hooks: install our tracing header and log forwarder; prepare your Datadog/AWS CloudWatch forwarder (2–3 days)
- Preflight tests: provide representative prompt sets + perf targets for KV warming (we’ll run and report)

Canary & rollback controls:
- Health checks: per-route p50/p95 latency, error rate, and token generation failures
- Automatic rollback: if p95 latency degrades >30% vs baseline or error rate >1% sustained for 5m, traffic shifts back to the previous provider
- TTR (time-to-restore target): <10 minutes for automated fallback; manual rollback playbook for complex failures (~30–60 minutes)

Artifacts we’ll supply: deployment manifests, canary telemetry dashboards, CSVs of pre/post latency distributions, test prompts and results, and post-cutover verification checklist.

Attachments: Redwood_Migration_Playbook_v1.pdf, Canary_Criteria.xlsx

Next steps: Laura (ops lead) will follow up with a staging checklist and a proposed rehearsal window. If that timeline works, we can produce a final playbook and evidence bundle by Thursday.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_Migration_Playbook_v1.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: Canary_Criteria.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Mike Chen <mike.chen@northbridge.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jamie Reynolds <jamie@northbridge.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 13:26:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: RFI: orchestration scheduling and hotpath fallback plan for migration

Ben/Team —

Couple of technical clarifications from our infra side before we sign off on candidate schedules: 

1) Data residency: during canary we need assured routing to our eu-west-1 region for EU-origin traffic; can Redwood pin instances by region and do weighted routing per geo?
2) KV cache warm-up: you mention warming with prompts — what are expected VM/GPU startup times and warm-up token counts to reach steady-state p95?
3) Monitoring hooks: can you provide the exact tracing header names and a sample Datadog dashboard JSON we can preload?
4) Fallback semantics: if an automated rollback occurs, do you provide a transparent diff of requests that failed/rolled back for reconciliation?

Also: procurement asked whether the rehearsal (dry-run) requires a maintenance window or can we use canary traffic (non-customer) during business hours.

-Mike
Lead Infrastructure Engineer
Northbridge Financial
[Attachment: none]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Chen <mike.chen@northbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:33:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: RFI: orchestration scheduling and hotpath fallback plan for migration

Mike — great questions. Answers below and I’ve embedded a concise staging-runbook (see attached staging-runbook-checklist.md) with specific ops steps.

1) Region pinning & routing: yes. We support regional endpoint pinning and weighted routing policies at the edge. For EU-origin traffic we’ll provision eu-west-1 Dedicated nodes and configure per-region traffic weights in our routing policy. We’ll provide the routing policy file and verification checklist.

2) KV warm-up and steady-state: typical GPU instance cold start is 90–180s (driver + model load) depending on quantization/profile. Practical warm-up to reach stable p95 requires ~1–3M tokens of representative traffic or targeted synthetic warm-up runs; for hotpath endpoints we recommend staged synthetic ramping over 24–48 hours plus a focused short-burst pre-canary run to validate p95 targets. We’ll share expected token counts per model profile in the final playbook.

3) Monitoring hooks: tracing header is X-Redwood-Trace; we provide a Datadog dashboard JSON export (link below) with per-route latency heatmaps, failure counts, and token distribution histograms. You can preload that before the canary.

4) Fallback diffs and reconciliation: on automated rollback we produce a reconciliation bundle (NDJSON) with request ids, timestamps, observed latency/error codes, and the traffic route decision. We’ll redact PII as needed and supply the bundle for your SREs to correlate.

Rehearsal: we recommend performing the rehearsal using non-customer sandbox traffic during a low-traffic window (overnight local time). That said, if you prefer canary-style rehearsal, we can limit to synthetic traffic and a 1% live traffic slice; procurement needs to sign off on risk acceptance.

Attachments: staging-runbook-checklist.md
Related Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-northbridge-runbooks, https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INF-4823

—Laura
Senior Manager, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
